question.text: Milestone Valuation in a Cat I/II AIF term sheet is used primarily because:

answer.text: VC investors want to reward founders for exceeding forecast
SEBI mandates milestone valuation for all Cat I AIF investments
Investors are uncertain about forecast-based valuation and prefer to peg valuation to technical/commercial targets; missing milestones can trigger a valuation downward revision or downround
Tax authorities require milestone valuation under Section 56(2)(viib)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Series XIX-C page 291, venture capital investors may not agree to forecast-based valuation and instead peg valuation to technical and/or commercial milestones. Missed milestones may lead to a downward revision in valuation, a downround, or a delay in future investments. The Trap: Option A inverts the rationale (milestones are a discipline mechanism, not a reward for exceeding forecast). Option B is incorrect because SEBI does not mandate milestone valuation for all Cat I AIF investments. Option D misreads tax law. Note: Anchor the answer on the milestone-pegged valuation logic and the downward-revision/downround/delay consequence described on page 291.
